[DEFINE_WORKER: "Constructs a square grid of dots, draws forward-slash and backslash paths based on mutated ball counts, returns the shortest non-empty row prefix prefixed by a dot row, or returns 'IMPOSSIBLE' when an endpoint ball count is zero." solve]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> B </REF>: list of integers "Non-empty list of non-negative integer ball counts; the list is mutated during execution."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> return_value </REF>: tuple "Either ('IMPOSSIBLE', None) on the early impossible path, or (len(ans), ans) where ans is a list of rows containing '.', '/', and backslash characters."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check the initial boundary condition: if B[0] == 0 or B[-1] == 0, take the alternative flow that returns 'IMPOSSIBLE' and None; otherwise continue. RESULT boundary_check_passed]
            [COMMAND Set C = len(B) and initialize grid as an empty list, discarding the earlier empty-list assignment. RESULT grid_and_C]
            [COMMAND Fill grid with C rows: for each j in range(C), create an empty row, append '.' to it C times using an inner loop over range(C), then append that row to grid. RESULT grid]
            [COMMAND Initialize shadowed using the source expression [False] * len(C), then set shadowed[0] = True. RESULT shadowed]
            [COMMAND Decrement B[0] by 1 and decrement B[-1] by 1. RESULT B]
            [COMMAND Set i = 0, then enter the for loop over i in range(C), so i takes values from 0 through C-1. RESULT i_loop]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over i, if B[i] == 0 and shadowed[i] is true, continue to the next i and skip the remaining steps for this iteration. RESULT skip_iteration]
            [COMMAND Within the same for-loop iteration, if B[i] > 0 and shadowed[i] is false, start the left pass: set unshadowed_balls = 0, j = i - 1, and l = 1; while j >= 1 and not shadowed[j], set grid[l][j] to a backslash, set shadowed[j] = True, increment unshadowed_balls and l, and decrement j. RESULT left_pass]
            [COMMAND After the left pass, if B[i] <= unshadowed_balls, set excess_balls = unshadowed_balls - B[i] + 1 and j = i; while excess_balls > 1, decrement j and excess_balls and set shadowed[j] = False. Otherwise, decrement B[i] by unshadowed_balls + 1 and set shadowed[i] = True. RESULT left_branch_update]
            [COMMAND Within the same for-loop iteration, if B[i] > 0 and shadowed[i] is true, including when the previous step just set it, initialize r = B[i], j = i + 1, and l = 1; while j < C - 1 and shadowed[j] is true, set grid[l][j] = '/', increment l and j, and leave r unchanged. RESULT right_existing_scan]
            [COMMAND Continue the right-side logic: while j < C - 1 and r > 0, set grid[l][j] = '/', set shadowed[j] = True, decrement r, and increment l and j. RESULT right_fill]
            [COMMAND After the for loop over i, initialize ans as an empty list. RESULT ans]
            [COMMAND For each index in range(1, C), set row = grid[index] and include_row = False; scan every cell in row, and if any cell equals a backslash or '/', set include_row = True and break. If include_row is true, append row to ans; otherwise break out of the loop. RESULT ans]
            [COMMAND Prepend a new dot row to ans by setting ans = [['.' for i in range(C)]] + ans. RESULT ans]
            [COMMAND Return the tuple (len(ans), ans). RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: B[0] == 0 or B[-1] == 0 at the initial boundary check]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the tuple ('IMPOSSIBLE', None) immediately, without modifying B or building the grid. RESULT impossible_return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
